sentences.text: The genus Kryptodrakon was named and described by Andres, Clark, and Xu in 2014, with the type species designated as Kryptodrakon progenitor.
The generic name Kryptodrakon means 'hidden dragon' in Greek, a title that alludes to the film Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, which was filmed near the fossil site.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of various wing and shoulder bones, including parts of the humerus, radius, metacarpals, and wing phalanges.
These bones were found unarticulated in a small 30 cm² area, likely representing a single individual.
Kryptodrakon had an estimated wingspan of 1.47 meters, and its slender and elongated fourth metacarpal indicates it is a pterodactyloid.
The fourth metacarpal is at least 7.22 cm long, while the humerus is estimated to be between 7.5 cm and 8.6 cm, and the radius has a unique feature: an extra lump on its front outer lower side.
The skeleton shows no signs of pneumatization, meaning the bones were solid rather than hollow.
Kryptodrakon is the oldest and most basal known pterodactyloid.
This creature is approximately five million years older than previously discovered pterodactyloids.
Fossil bones of Kryptodrakon were discovered in Xinjiang in 2001 by Chris Sloan, but the fossils were initially mistaken for a theropod dinosaur before James Clark identified them as a pterosaur.

Brian Andres, James Clark, and Xu Xing formally named the species Kryptodrakon progenitor in 2014, and the holotype specimen dates to the Callovian–Oxfordian stages with a minimum age of 161 million years.
Kryptodrakon lived in a terrestrial habitat far from the coast, and researchers suggest that this terrestrial habitat indicates a terrestrial origin for the Pterodactyloidea.
The relatively short wings of Kryptodrakon support the hypothesis that short-winged species inhabit forests while long-winged species live near coasts.
Kryptodrakon lived during the Middle to Late Jurassic, approximately 162.7 million years ago.
More specifically, Kryptodrakon lived from 161.5 to 154.8 million years ago during the Oxfordian stage.
It is debated whether a previously described Middle Jurassic jaw from the UK is a pterosaur or a teleosaurid stem-crocodilian.
